test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated user is redirected from the Tags page
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Tags page URL without being logged in.
test_cases.expected: The browser redirects to the login page. The Tags list is not shown.

test_cases.scenario: Authenticated user can view the Tags list
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as any user.
2. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
test_cases.expected: The Tags page loads and the tag list is visible. The page is read-only — no add, edit, or delete actions are available.

test_cases.scenario: Export button is only visible to users with 'can_export_tag' permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with the 'can_export_tag' permission.
2. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
test_cases.expected: The Export button is visible in the page header.

test_cases.scenario: Export button is not visible without the 'can_export_tag' permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without the 'can_export_tag' permission.
2. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
test_cases.expected: The Export button is not present in the page header.

test_cases.scenario: No row actions are available on the Tags page
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
2. Hover over or tap a tag row.
test_cases.expected: No action buttons (edit, delete, toggle, etc.) appear on any row. Tags are read-only; they can only be browsed and exported.

test_cases.scenario: Tags page loads with the correct layout and table
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
test_cases.expected: The page shows the 'Administration' eyebrow, 'Tags' heading, and subtitle 'Browse and export tags used across the platform.' The filter panel and table are visible with columns: Tag, Code, Created, Created By.

test_cases.scenario: Search filters the tag list by name
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
2. Type a partial tag name in the search field.
test_cases.expected: Only tags whose names match the search input are shown in the table.

test_cases.scenario: Pressing '/' keyboard shortcut focuses the search field
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
2. Press '/' on the keyboard.
test_cases.expected: The search field receives keyboard focus.

test_cases.scenario: Table can be sorted by the Tag (name) column
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
2. Click the 'Tag' column header.
test_cases.expected: Tags are sorted alphabetically by name. Clicking again reverses the direction.

test_cases.scenario: Table can be sorted by the Created column
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
2. Click the 'Created' column header.
test_cases.expected: Tags are sorted by creation date. Clicking again reverses the direction.

test_cases.scenario: Code column displays in monospace style
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
2. Look at the Code column values.
test_cases.expected: The Code column displays tag codes in a monospace font, visually distinct from the Tag name column.

test_cases.scenario: Pagination loads more tags when there are more than 25
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags when there are more than 25 tags.
2. Scroll to the bottom of the table.
test_cases.expected: Pagination controls appear. Clicking the next page loads the next set of tags.

test_cases.scenario: Empty state shown when search returns no tags
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
2. Enter a search term that matches no tag.
test_cases.expected: 'No tags found.' is displayed in the table area.

test_cases.scenario: Created By column shows the user who created each tag
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
2. View the Created By column.
test_cases.expected: The Created By column displays the name or identifier of the user who created each tag.

test_cases.scenario: Tags list reflects all tags used across the platform
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
2. Create a tag in another module (e.g., by tagging a project).
3. Return to the Tags page.
test_cases.expected: The newly created tag is visible in the Tags list. The page aggregates tags from across the entire platform.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Export opens the export panel
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with 'can_export_tag' permission.
2. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
3. Click the 'Export' button.
test_cases.expected: An export configuration panel or drawer opens.

test_cases.scenario: Export respects the active search filter
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
2. Search for tags matching a specific term.
3. Click 'Export' and download the file.
test_cases.expected: The exported file contains only tags matching the current search filter, not all tags in the system.

test_cases.scenario: Export file downloads successfully with expected columns
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags.
2. Click 'Export' and confirm the export.
test_cases.expected: A file is downloaded. It contains at minimum: tag name, code, created date, and created by.

test_cases.scenario: Export with empty result (no tags matching filter) handles gracefully
test_cases.steps:
1. Apply a search filter that returns no tags.
2. Click 'Export'.
test_cases.expected: The export either produces a file with headers only, or shows a message that there are no tags to export. No error or crash occurs.

test_cases.scenario: Tags page loads within an acceptable time
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Administration > Tags when many tags exist across the platform.
test_cases.expected: The page and table load within 3 seconds. Pagination handles large datasets.

test_cases.scenario: Tags page is read-only — no create, edit, or delete functionality exists
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Administration > Tags as an admin user.
2. Try to find a way to create, edit, or delete a tag from this page.
test_cases.expected: No such actions exist on the Tags page. Tags are managed implicitly through other platform features (e.g., tagging projects or work items). The Tags page is purely for visibility and export.

test_cases.scenario: Session expiry redirects to login
test_cases.steps:
1. Let the session expire while on the Tags page.
2. Attempt to interact with the page.
test_cases.expected: The browser redirects to the login page.

test_cases.scenario: All table columns are visible on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. Open Administration > Tags on a desktop browser (1280px+ wide).
test_cases.expected: Tag, Code, Created, and Created By columns are all visible.

test_cases.scenario: Code column renders at fixed width (140px) on desktop
test_cases.steps:
1. Open Administration > Tags on a desktop browser.
2. Check the Code column width.
test_cases.expected: The Code column is fixed at approximately 140px wide. Long codes are not cut off at this width.

test_cases.scenario: Only the Tag column is visible in the table on mobile
test_cases.steps: 1. Open Administration > Tags on a mobile device or narrow viewport.
test_cases.expected: Only the Tag (name) column is visible. Code, Created, and Created By (all hide-mobile) are hidden.

test_cases.scenario: Search field is accessible on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. Open Administration > Tags on a mobile device.
2. Tap the search field.
test_cases.expected: The search field is easily tappable and the keyboard appears. Searching updates the tag list.

test_cases.scenario: Export button is accessible on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. Open Administration > Tags on a mobile device.
2. Locate and tap the Export button.
test_cases.expected: The Export button is visible and tappable in the page header. Tapping it opens the export panel.
